body:
`cps/db.py` `setup_db`, DESKTOP_COMPAT_MODE branch.

The branch logs, unconditionally:

    "DESKTOP_COMPAT_MODE=true: using per-request SQLite connections. "
    "calibre desktop can access the library between web requests. "
    "WAL mode remains disabled (NETWORK_SHARE_MODE behaviour)."

but the code that actually converts the database to DELETE journal mode is
gated on `if nsm and db_writable:` — i.e. it only runs when NETWORK_SHARE_MODE
is ALSO set.

`journal_mode` is persisted in the SQLite file header (MEASURED: set WAL, close
every connection, reopen in a fresh process -> still reports `wal`). So on the
common upgrade path — user runs normally for a while, the library becomes WAL,
then they set DESKTOP_COMPAT_MODE=true to let calibre desktop in — the library
stays in WAL and the log asserts the opposite.

Neither branch *sets* WAL when desktop_compat is true, so nothing regresses; the
defect is that the log states a mode it never established. An operator reading
it to diagnose a calibre-desktop coexistence problem is told the wrong thing.

Fix shape: either extend the conversion to `if db_writable:` inside the branch,
or make the log report the journal mode it actually observed. The second is
safer — the code comment above the conversion warns that per-connection mode
switches checkpoint the WAL and can destroy frames another writer wrote, so
converting unconditionally is not obviously correct on a local library.

Adjacent, same code path, lower value: `db_writable = os.access(dbpath, os.W_OK)`
checks the *file*, but WAL must create `-wal`/`-shm` in the *directory*. MEASURED
(uid 1000, dir 0555, writable db file): the pragma fails with "attempt to write a
readonly database", the surrounding `except Exception: pass` swallows it, and the
database correctly stays in DELETE. Self-protecting, so no user-visible bug — but
the gate does not mean what it reads like it means.
title: DESKTOP_COMPAT_MODE logs 'WAL mode remains disabled' without ever converting an existing WAL library back to DELETE
